editorial:
Imagine trying to raise a kid who just doesn't care about anything, but has a hunger that never goes away. You follow a stressed-out single mom who is doing her best to connect with her son, Joe. The vibe is pretty heavy and awkward from the start. You can feel how tired the mother is as she tries to feed a boy who eats everything in sight but remains totally cold and distant. It is a slow burn that makes you feel uneasy because you know something is very wrong with the boy, but you cannot quite put your finger on it until things get really messy.

The acting is the best part here because it makes the weird family dynamic feel real. While some parts of the story drag a bit, the shock value at the end makes the wait worth it. If you like movies that make you squirm, you should definitely give this one a go. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want to add it to your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a rainy night when you want something strange.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the reveal that Joe is not a normal human. His hunger becomes impossible to satisfy with regular food, leading him to eat people. The mother tries to protect him for too long, but eventually, Joe's nature takes over completely. He turns on everyone around him to feed his bottomless stomach. The story wraps up with a dark realization that some monsters are born, and no amount of love can fix them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird indie horror movies with a dark twist.
